subject: Polity
topic: Local government and Panchayati Raj — mixed tiers
description: 73rd & 74th Amendments, three-tier system, reservation, eligibility, urban bodies

questions.stem: Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) became constitutionally mandated through the:
questions.explanation: 73rd Amendment 1992 — added Part IX (Articles 243-243-O) and 11th Schedule (29 subjects). Mandatory three-tier system (village + intermediate + district) for states with population > 20 lakh. 5-year tenure. Direct elections. Reservation for SC/ST/Women (1/3 → 50% in 20 states). 73rd's urban counterpart — 74th Amendment (Part IX-A, 12th Schedule, 18 subjects) — added municipalities. Both came into force on the same day — 1 June 1993.

questions.stem: Article 243G provides for the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats. The 11th Schedule lists how many subjects?
questions.explanation: 11th Schedule (Article 243G) — 29 subjects suggested for devolution to Panchayats: agriculture, animal husbandry, primary education, health, drinking water, rural housing, women & child welfare etc. 12th Schedule (Article 243W) — 18 subjects for Municipalities (urban local bodies): urban planning, sanitation, water supply, slums etc. Implementation varies by state — some have devolved many, some not. PRIs typically face shortage of funds, functions, functionaries (the '3F' problem).

questions.stem: The minimum age to contest a Panchayat / Municipality election is:
questions.explanation: Article 243F (Panchayats) and Article 243V (Municipalities) — qualifications: (1) registered as voter (so 18 years voting age); (2) attained 21 years of age. So minimum age to CONTEST = 21. Compare: MP/MLA = 25 years; Rajya Sabha / State Council = 30; President / VP / Governor = 35. Disqualifications similar to RPA — corrupt practices, bankruptcy, etc. Some states (Rajasthan, Haryana) added qualifications like minimum education and toilet at home (controversial; SC upheld 2015).

questions.stem: The 'Three-Tier' Panchayati Raj structure consists of:

options.option_text: Gram Panchayat (village) + Panchayat Samiti / Mandal Parishad (block) + Zila Parishad (district)

questions.explanation: Three-tier system mandated by 73rd Amendment (states with population > 20 lakh). VILLAGE level — Gram Panchayat (head — Sarpanch). BLOCK level — Panchayat Samiti / Janpad / Mandal Parishad. DISTRICT level — Zila Parishad / Zila Panchayat (head — Adhyaksha or President). States < 20 lakh population may have only village + district levels. Balwantrai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended 3-tier; Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) — 2-tier (Mandal + Zila); only the former was institutionalised.

questions.stem: The State Election Commission (different from ECI) handles elections to:
questions.explanation: Article 243K (Panchayats) + 243ZA (Municipalities) — superintendence, direction and control of elections to Panchayats / Municipalities is vested in the STATE Election Commission. SEC is a constitutional body (different from ECI which handles Centre + State Legislature elections). State EC appointed by Governor. Removable like a HC judge. Goa SEC vs Fouzia Imtiaz Shaikh (2021) reaffirmed SEC's autonomy from State govt. Some states have very strong SECs (Karnataka, Kerala); others perceived weaker.

questions.stem: The 74th Amendment Act 1992 introduced THREE types of Urban Local Bodies. They are:

options.option_text: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad
Nagar Panchayat (transitional area), Municipal Council (smaller urban area), Municipal Corporation (larger urban area)

questions.explanation: Article 243Q — 3 types of Municipal bodies based on population: (a) Nagar Panchayat — for areas in transition from rural to urban (typically < 25,000 population); (b) Municipal Council — smaller urban (25,000 - 1 lakh); (c) Municipal Corporation — large city (> 3 lakh). Numbers vary by state laws. Special bodies like Notified Area Committee, Town Area Committee, Cantonment Board, Township, Port Trust, Special Purpose Agency exist for specific contexts but are NOT under 74th's three-tier.

questions.stem: The first state to introduce the 3-tier Panchayati Raj system on 2 October 1959 (Gandhi Jayanti) — preceding the 73rd Amendment — was:
questions.explanation: Rajasthan's Nagaur district — PM Nehru launched first 3-tier Panchayati Raj on 2 October 1959. Andhra Pradesh — second (1959). Karnataka was a pioneer in implementing reforms in early 1980s under CM Ramakrishna Hegde. Pre-73rd Amendment, Panchayats existed under State laws (often weak, irregular elections). The Constitution merely had Article 40 (DPSP — 'organise village panchayats') — non-justiciable. 73rd Amendment elevated PRIs to constitutional status.
